limits: The agent is a stand-in, not Lorikeet's Concierge. Each reply came from a fresh Claude Sonnet sub-agent that saw only the SOP and the caller's words. It never saw the rules or the checks.

Grading was blind to the SOP. A separate Claude grader saw only the caller, the reply, the logged actions and the checks. The bare-bones runs were shuffled together, round 1 mixed draft and Fix 1 replies under shuffled IDs, and round 2 was graded in its own pass. Every verdict carries the quote it was based on, and I spot-checked the grader against the replies.
Few samples. The bare-bones SOP ran twice per scenario; each flawed and fixed SOP ran once. Model output varies run to run, so treat these as small samples, not rates.
Single-turn calls. Each scenario is the caller's opening message and the agent's first reply. Real calls go back and forth, which is where some failures hide.
Scope. Debit card and checking account disputes under Regulation E only. Credit cards (Regulation Z), EBT benefits, and the special prepaid-account rules are out of scope.
Not legal advice. Rules are quoted from the regulation, its official interpretation and CFPB's FAQ, but a real deployment needs the customer's compliance team to review the checks.
